title.zh: 卷350 列傳一百三十七 李长庚子：廷钰 胡振声 王得禄 邱良功 陈步雲 许松年 黄标 林国良 许廷桂
title.en: Volume 350 Biographies 137: Li Changgeng son: Ting Yu, Hu Zhensheng, Wang Delu, Qiu Lianggong, Chen Buyun, Xu Songnian, Huang Biao, Lin Guoliang, Xu Tinggui
title.raw: 卷350 列傳一百三十七 李长庚子：廷钰 胡振声 王得禄 邱良功 陈步雲 许松年 黄标 林国良 许廷桂

sentences.zh: 列傳一百三十七

translations.literal: Biographies 137.
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 137

sentences.zh: 李長庚子廷鈺胡振聲王得祿邱良功陳步雲

translations.literal: Li Changgeng, his son Tingyu, Hu Zhensheng, Wang Delu, Qiu Lianggong, and Chen Buyun.
translations.idiomatic: Li Changgeng, his son Tingyu, Hu Zhensheng, Wang Delu, Qiu Lianggong, and Chen Buyun

sentences.zh: 許松年黃標林國良許廷桂

translations.literal: Xu Songnian, Huang Biao, Lin Guoliang, and Xu Tinggui.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Songnian, Huang Biao, Lin Guoliang, and Xu Tinggui

sentences.zh: 李長庚，字西岩，福建同安人。

translations.literal: Li Changgeng, style name Xiyan, was a native of Tong'an in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Li Changgeng, whose style was Xiyan, came from Tong'an in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十六年武進士，授藍翎侍衛。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year of Qianlong he passed the military examinations and was appointed a Blue Bordered Bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 36 he took his degree as a military licentiate and was appointed a Blue Bordered Bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 出為浙江衢州營都司，累遷樂清協副將。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as battalion commander of the Quzhou Garrison in Zhejiang and was repeatedly promoted to deputy commander of the Yueqing Brigade.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as battalion commander of the Quzhou Garrison in Zhejiang and rose in due course to deputy commander of the Yueqing Brigade.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，署福建海壇鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year he served as acting commander of the Haitan Garrison in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In year 52 he acted as commander of the Haitan Garrison in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 鄰海有盜，誤指所轄界，坐褫職。

translations.literal: Pirates appeared off a neighboring coast and were wrongly said to be within his jurisdiction; he was dismissed from office on that account.
translations.idiomatic: When pirates struck a neighboring stretch of coast, he was wrongly blamed for their operating within his jurisdiction and was stripped of his post.

sentences.zh: 罄家財募鄉勇，捕獲巨盜，起用，補海壇游擊，遷銅山參將。

translations.literal: He spent his entire family fortune to raise local militia, captured a major pirate, was reinstated, was made up to guerrilla colonel at Haitan, and was transferred to brigade general at Tongshan.
translations.idiomatic: He poured his family fortune into raising local militia, captured a major pirate leader, was reinstated, filled the post of guerrilla colonel at Haitan, and was promoted to brigade general at Tongshan.

sentences.zh: 自乾隆季年，安南內亂，招瀕海亡命劫內洋，以濟餉為患，粵東土盜鳳尾、水澳兩幫附之，遂益肆擾。

translations.literal: From the closing years of Qianlong, Annam was torn by civil war and recruited coastal desperadoes to raid the inner seas to supply its armies, which became a grave menace; the Guangdong pirate bands Fengwei and Shui'ao attached themselves to them, and depredations grew worse.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Qianlong years civil war in Annam drew coastal outlaws into raids on the inner seas to provision its armies, and the Guangdong bands Fengwei and Shui'ao joined them, so that piracy grew far worse.

sentences.zh: 五十九年，夷艇始犯福建三澎，長庚擊走之。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year foreign rebel vessels first attacked the three Pescadores off Fujian; Changgeng drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: In year 59 foreign rebel junks first struck the three Pescadores off Fujian, and Changgeng beat them back.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶二年，遷澎湖協副將，擢浙江定海鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiaqing he was transferred to deputy commander of the Penghu Brigade and was promoted to commander of the Dinghai Garrison in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 2 he became deputy commander of the Penghu Brigade and was promoted to commander of the Dinghai Garrison in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 三年，迭擊洋匪於衢港及普陀。

translations.literal: In the third year he repeatedly attacked sea bandits at Qu Port and Putuo.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he fought sea bandits again and again at Qu Port and Putuo.

sentences.zh: 四年，鳳尾幫引夷艇入溫州洋，敗之，賜花翎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the Fengwei band led foreign rebel vessels into the seas off Wenzhou; he defeated them and was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 the Fengwei band brought foreign rebel junks into Wenzhou waters; he defeated them and was awarded the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 五年夏，夷艇合水澳、鳳尾百餘艘萃於浙洋，逼台州。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fifth year more than a hundred foreign rebel vessels together with the Shui'ao and Fengwei bands gathered in Zhejiang waters and pressed on Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: That summer more than a hundred foreign rebel craft, together with the Shui'ao and Fengwei bands, massed in Zhejiang waters and threatened Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 巡撫阮元奏以長庚總統三鎮水師擊之，會師海門。

translations.literal: Governor Ruan Yuan memorialized that Changgeng should take overall command of the naval forces of the three garrisons to attack them, and the fleets assembled at Haimen.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Ruan Yuan asked that Changgeng be given overall command of the three garrisons' fleets; the squadrons rendezvoused at Haimen.

sentences.zh: 賊泊松門山下相持，颶風大作，覆溺幾盡，其泊岸及附敗舟者皆就俘，獲安南偽侯倫貴利等四總兵，磔之，以敕印擲還其國。

translations.literal: The rebels anchored below Songmen Mountain and faced off; a typhoon rose and nearly all were capsized and drowned. Those who reached shore or clung to wrecked boats were all taken prisoner. Four Annamese false marquises including Lun Guili were captured, dismembered, and their imperial seals were thrown back to their country.
translations.idiomatic: The pirates lay at anchor below Songmen Mountain in a stalemate until a typhoon struck and nearly wiped them out. Every man who made shore or clung to a wreck was taken. Four rebel "marquises" of Annam, including Lun Guili, were captured and executed by dismemberment, and their imperial seals were sent back to their country.

sentences.zh: 是年，擢福建水師提督，尋調浙江。

translations.literal: That year he was promoted to naval commander-in-chief of Fujian and soon transferred to Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was made naval commander-in-chief of Fujian and soon after was transferred to Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 安南烏艚船百餘號，總兵十二人，分前中後三隊，所獲四總兵，其後隊也。

translations.literal: The Annamese had more than a hundred black war-junks and twelve brigade generals divided into front, middle, and rear squadrons; the four generals captured were from the rear squadron.
translations.idiomatic: The Annamese force had numbered more than a hundred black war-junks and twelve brigade generals in three squadrons; the four generals taken had belonged to the rear squadron.

sentences.zh: 未幾，安南新阮內附，受封守約束，艇匪無所巢穴。

translations.literal: Before long the new Nguyen regime in Annam submitted and accepted investiture and restraint, and the rebel vessels had no refuge.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the new Nguyen court in Annam submitted to the Qing, accepted investiture, and kept its people in check, so the rebel fleets lost their havens.

sentences.zh: 其在閩者，皆為漳盜蔡牽所並，有艇百餘，粵盜硃濆亦得數十艘。

translations.literal: Those remaining in Fujian were all absorbed by the Zhangzhou pirate Cai Qian, who had more than a hundred vessels; the Guangdong pirate Zhu Fen also obtained several dozen.
translations.idiomatic: Those who remained in Fujian were absorbed by the Zhangzhou pirate Cai Qian, who commanded more than a hundred junks; the Guangdong pirate Zhu Fen took several dozen for his own.

sentences.zh: 牽，同安人，奸猾善用眾，既得夷艇，凡水澳、鳳尾諸黨悉歸之，遂猖獗。

translations.literal: Qian was a native of Tong'an, cunning and skilled at commanding men; once he had foreign rebel vessels, all the Shui'ao, Fengwei, and other bands submitted to him, and he grew rampant.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Qian came from Tong'an. Cunning and adept at leading large forces, he won the foreign rebel junks and drew every Shui'ao and Fengwei band to his banner, after which his raids became relentless.

sentences.zh: 阮元與長庚議夷艇高大，水師戰艦不能制，乃集捐十餘萬金付長庚，赴閩造大艦三十，名曰霆船，鑄大砲四百餘配之。

translations.literal: Ruan Yuan and Changgeng discussed how the foreign rebel vessels were tall and large and the navy's warships could not master them; they therefore raised more than a hundred thousand taels in donations for Changgeng, who went to Fujian to build thirty large ships called Thunder Ships and cast more than four hundred great guns to equip them.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Yuan and Changgeng agreed that the foreign rebel junks were too tall for the regular war fleet to overcome. More than a hundred thousand taels were raised and entrusted to Changgeng, who went to Fujian to build thirty large men-of-war called Thunder Ships and fit them with more than four hundred heavy guns.

sentences.zh: 連敗牽等於海上，軍威大振。

translations.literal: He repeatedly defeated Qian and others at sea, and military prestige rose greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated Cai Qian again and again at sea, and the navy's prestige soared.

sentences.zh: 八年，牽竄定海，進香普陀山，長庚掩至，牽僅以身免，窮追至閩洋，賊船糧盡帆壞，偽乞降於總督玉德，遣興泉永道慶徠赴三沙招撫，玉德遽檄浙師收港，牽得以其間修船揚帆去。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Qian fled to Dinghai and went to burn incense at Mount Putuo; Changgeng fell upon him by surprise and Qian barely escaped with his life. Pursued to Fujian waters, the rebel ships ran out of grain and their sails were ruined; he feigned surrender to Governor Yude, who sent the Xing-Quan-Yong circuit intendant Qing Lai to Sansha to offer amnesty. Yude hastily ordered the Zhejiang fleet to withdraw to port, and Qian used the interval to repair his ships and sail away.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 Cai Qian slipped into Dinghai and went to offer incense at Mount Putuo. Changgeng surprised him, and Qian barely escaped alive. Changgeng chased him into Fujian waters until the pirate fleet was starving and its sails in tatters. Qian then pretended to surrender to Governor Yude, who sent Intendant Qing Lai to Sansha to negotiate. Yude abruptly ordered the Zhejiang fleet back to harbor, and Qian used the respite to refit his ships and escape.

sentences.zh: 浙師追擊於三沙及溫州，毀其船六。

translations.literal: The Zhejiang fleet pursued and attacked at Sansha and Wenzhou, destroying six of his ships.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhejiang fleet pursued him at Sansha and Wenzhou and destroyed six of his ships.

sentences.zh: 牽畏霆船，賄閩商造大艇，高於霆船，出洋以被劫報，牽得之，渡橫洋，劫台灣米以餉硃濆，遂與之合。

translations.literal: Qian feared the Thunder Ships, bribed Fujian merchants to build large junks taller than the Thunder Ships, sent them to sea and reported them as having been seized, obtained them, crossed the open ocean, plundered Taiwan rice to supply Zhu Fen, and then joined forces with him.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the Thunder Ships, Qian bribed Fujian merchants to build junks even larger, sent them to sea under false reports of capture, took possession of them, crossed the open ocean, raided Taiwan for rice to supply Zhu Fen, and finally joined Zhu's band.

sentences.zh: 九年夏，連宗八十餘入閩，戕總兵胡振聲，詔治閩將不援罪，長庚總統兩省水師。

translations.literal: In the summer of the ninth year more than eighty of the Lian clan entered Fujian and killed Brigade General Hu Zhensheng; an edict punished the Fujian commanders for failing to aid him, and Changgeng took overall command of the naval forces of both provinces.
translations.idiomatic: That summer more than eighty members of the Lian clan entered Fujian and killed Brigade General Hu Zhensheng. The court punished Fujian officers who had failed to relieve him and placed Changgeng in overall command of the fleets of both provinces.

sentences.zh: 秋，牽、濆共犯浙，長庚合諸鎮兵擊之於定海北洋，衝賊為二，自當牽，急擊，逐至盡山。

translations.literal: In autumn Qian and Fen jointly invaded Zhejiang; Changgeng combined the forces of the garrisons and attacked them in the northern sea off Dinghai, splitting the rebels in two. He himself faced Qian, pressed the attack hotly, and pursued him to Jinshan.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Cai Qian and Zhu Fen raided Zhejiang together. Changgeng united the garrison fleets and met them in the northern sea off Dinghai, splitting the pirate force in two. He took Qian on himself, pressed hard, and chased him as far as Jinshan.

sentences.zh: 牽以大艇得遁，委敗硃濆，濆怒，於是復分。

translations.literal: Qian escaped in his large junk and abandoned Zhu Fen to defeat; Fen was enraged, and the two bands separated again.
translations.idiomatic: Qian escaped in his great junk and left Zhu Fen to bear the defeat. Zhu Fen was furious, and the two bands parted ways once more.

sentences.zh: 十年夏，調福建提督。

translations.literal: In the summer of the tenth year he was transferred to be naval commander-in-chief of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of year 10 he was made naval commander-in-chief of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 牽聞長庚至，遂竄浙，追敗之青龍港，又敗之於台州斗米洋。

translations.literal: When Qian heard that Changgeng had arrived, he fled into Zhejiang; Changgeng pursued and defeated him at Qinglong Harbor and again at Doumiyang off Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Changgeng had come, Cai Qian fled into Zhejiang. Changgeng pursued him, defeated him at Qinglong Harbor, and beat him again at Doumiyang off Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 復調浙江提督。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to be naval commander-in-chief of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred back to naval commander-in-chief of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 十一年正月，牽合百餘艘犯台灣，結土匪萬餘攻府城，自號鎮海王，沉舟鹿耳門阻援兵。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eleventh year Qian gathered more than a hundred vessels and invaded Taiwan, joined more than ten thousand local bandits to attack the prefectural city, styled himself King Who Pacifies the Sea, and sank ships at Lu'ermen to block relief forces.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 11 Cai Qian led more than a hundred ships against Taiwan, rallied more than ten thousand local bandits to besiege the prefectural seat, called himself King Who Pacifies the Sea, and sank ships in Lu'ermen to block reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 長庚至，不得入，諜知南汕、北汕、大港門可通小舟，遣總兵許松年、副將王得祿繞道入，攻洲仔尾，連敗之。

translations.literal: When Changgeng arrived he could not enter; spies learned that Nanshan, Beishan, and Dagangmen could be reached by small boats. He sent Brigade General Xu Songnian and Deputy Commander Wang Delu in by a detour to attack Zhouzaiwei and repeatedly defeated the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Changgeng arrived but could not force an entrance. Scouts reported that small boats could pass through Nanshan, Beishan, and Dagangmen. He sent Brigade General Xu Songnian and Deputy Commander Wang Delu around by those routes to strike Zhouzaiwei and beat the pirates again and again.

sentences.zh: 二月，松年登洲仔尾，焚其藔，牽反救，長庚遣兵出南汕，與松年夾擊，大敗之。

translations.literal: In the second month Songnian landed at Zhouzaiwei and burned their stockades; Qian turned back to relieve them, and Changgeng sent troops out from Nanshan to attack in concert with Songnian, inflicting a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Xu Songnian stormed Zhouzaiwei and burned the pirate camps. Cai Qian turned back to relieve them, but Changgeng sent men out through Nanshan to join Xu in a pincer and routed the rebels.

sentences.zh: 牽無去路，困守北汕。

translations.literal: Qian had no way out and was trapped defending Beishan.
translations.idiomatic: With no escape left, Cai Qian was trapped at Beishan.

sentences.zh: 會風潮驟漲，沉舟漂起，乃奪鹿耳門逸去，詔奪花翎、頂戴。

translations.literal: Just then wind and tide surged; the sunken ships floated up, and he seized Lu'ermen and escaped. An edict stripped Changgeng of his peacock feather and official insignia.
translations.idiomatic: Then wind and tide rose sharply, the scuttled ships floated free, and he broke out through Lu'ermen. The court stripped Changgeng of his peacock feather and rank insignia.

sentences.zh: 四月，蔡牽、硃濆同犯福寧外洋，擊敗之，追至台州斗米洋，擒其黨李按等。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Cai Qian and Zhu Fen jointly raided the outer sea off Funing; he defeated them, pursued them to Doumiyang off Taizhou, and captured their followers Li An and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Cai Qian and Zhu Fen raided together off Funing. Changgeng defeated them, chased them to Doumiyang off Taizhou, and captured followers including Li An.

sentences.zh: 長庚疏言：「蔡逆未能殲擒者，實由兵船不得力，接濟未斷絕所致。

translations.literal: Changgeng memorialized: "The reason the rebel Cai has not been destroyed and captured is in truth that our war vessels are inadequate and supplies from shore have not been cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Changgeng wrote in a memorial: "The rebel Cai has not been destroyed chiefly because our warships are too weak and shore supplies to the pirates have never been cut off.

sentences.zh: 臣所乘之船，較各鎮為最大，及逼近牽船，尚低五六尺。

translations.literal: The ship Your servant sails is the largest of all the garrisons', yet when we close with Qian's vessel it is still five or six feet lower.
translations.idiomatic: Even the ship I command—the largest in the fleet—is still five or six feet lower than Cai Qian's when we close to board.

sentences.zh: 曾與三鎮總兵原預支養廉，捐造大船十五號，而督臣以造船需數月之久，借帑四五萬之多，不肯具奏。

translations.literal: Your servant once joined the three garrison commanders in advancing their salary stipends to donate funds to build fifteen large ships, but the governor argued that shipbuilding would take many months and borrowing forty or fifty thousand taels from the treasury was too much, and refused to memorialize it.
translations.idiomatic: I once joined the three garrison commanders in advancing our stipends to fund fifteen large ships, but the governor refused to memorialize the plan, saying construction would take months and a treasury loan of forty or fifty thousand taels was too costly.

sentences.zh: 且海賊無兩年不修之船，亦無一年不壞之槓料。

translations.literal: Moreover, sea pirates have no ships that go two years without repair, nor spars and timbers that last a year without replacement.
translations.idiomatic: Pirates, moreover, never let a ship go two years without repair or keep spars and timbers a full year without renewal.

sentences.zh: 桅柁折則船為虛器，風篷爛則寸步難行。

translations.literal: If mast and rudder break, the ship is an empty shell; if sails rot, it cannot move an inch.
translations.idiomatic: Break the mast or rudder and a ship is useless; let the sails rot and it cannot stir.

sentences.zh: 乃逆賊在鹿耳門竄出，僅餘船三十，篷朽硝缺；

translations.literal: Yet when the rebel fled from Lu'ermen he had only thirty ships left, with rotten sails and lacking gunpowder;
translations.idiomatic: Yet when the rebel broke out of Lu'ermen he had only thirty ships, with rotten sails and scarce powder;

sentences.zh: 一回閩地，裝篷燂洗，煥然一新，糧藥充足，賊何日可滅？

translations.literal: once back in Fujian he fitted new sails, caulked and washed his ships until they were wholly renewed, and had full stores of grain and munitions—on what day can the pirates be destroyed?
translations.idiomatic: once back in Fujian he re-rigged, caulked, and refitted until his fleet looked new again and his grain and powder were full—how then can the pirates ever be destroyed?"

sentences.zh: 」詔逮治玉德，以阿林保代。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered Yude arrested and punished; Alinbao replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Governor Yude arrested and replaced by Alinbao.

sentences.zh: 既至福建，諸文武吏以未協剿、未斷岸姦接濟、懼得罪​​，交譖長庚。

translations.literal: When he reached Fujian, civil and military officials, fearing punishment for failing to cooperate in suppression, failing to cut off shore collusion and supplies, slandered Changgeng to one another.
translations.idiomatic: Once in Fujian, civil and military officers who feared blame for poor cooperation and for letting shore suppliers feed the pirates joined in slandering Changgeng.

sentences.zh: 阿林保密劾其逗留，章三上，詔密詢浙江巡撫清安泰。

translations.literal: Alinbao secretly impeached him for delay; three memorials were sent up, and an edict secretly asked Zhejiang Governor Qing Antai.
translations.idiomatic: Alinbao secretly accused him of stalling; three memorials went up, and the throne privately asked Zhejiang Governor Qing Antai for the truth.

sentences.zh: 清安泰疏言：「長庚熟海島形勢、風雲沙線，每戰自持柁，老於操舟者不及。

translations.literal: Qing Antai memorialized: "Changgeng knows the shapes of the islands, the winds and clouds, and the sandbanks; in every battle he takes the helm himself, and veterans of seamanship cannot match him.
translations.idiomatic: Qing Antai replied: "Changgeng knows every island, wind pattern, and shoal. In every battle he takes the helm himself, and men who have sailed all their lives cannot match him.

sentences.zh: 兩年在軍，過門不入。

translations.literal: For two years in the army he passed his own door without entering.
translations.idiomatic: For two years on campaign he passed his own gate without going in.

sentences.zh: 以捐造船械，傾其家貲。

translations.literal: To donate funds for ships and weapons he exhausted his family fortune.
translations.idiomatic: He spent his family fortune building ships and arms for the fleet.

sentences.zh: 所俘獲盡以賞功，士爭效死。

translations.literal: Everything captured he gave entirely as rewards for merit, and the troops vied to die for the cause.
translations.idiomatic: Every prize he took went straight to reward merit, and his men vied to fight to the death.

sentences.zh: 八月中戰漁山，圍攻蔡逆，火器瓦石雨下，身受多創，將士傷百四十人，鏖戰不退。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he fought at Yushan, besieging the rebel Cai; firearms and stones rained down; he received many wounds himself and a hundred and forty officers and men were hurt, yet they fought on without retreating.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month at Yushan he besieged the rebel Cai under a rain of shot and stones. He was badly wounded, a hundred and forty of his men were hurt, yet they fought on without yielding.

sentences.zh: 賊中語：'不畏千萬兵，只畏李長庚。

translations.literal: Among the rebels they said: 'We do not fear millions of troops, we only fear Li Changgeng.
translations.idiomatic: Among the pirates they said, 'We do not fear millions of soldiers—we only fear Li Changgeng.

sentences.zh: '實水師諸將之冠。

translations.literal: ' He is truly the foremost of all naval commanders.
translations.idiomatic: ' He is truly the foremost commander of the fleet.

sentences.zh: 」且備陳海戰之難，非兩省合力不能成功狀。

translations.literal: " He also set forth in detail how difficult naval warfare was and that success was impossible unless the two provinces combined their strength.
translations.idiomatic: He also explained at length how hard naval warfare was and that neither province could succeed alone.

sentences.zh: 時同戰諸鎮，亦交章言長庚實非逗留。

translations.literal: At that time the garrison commanders who had fought alongside him also submitted memorials saying Changgeng had in fact not been delaying.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison commanders who had fought with him likewise wrote that Changgeng had not been stalling.

sentences.zh: 仁宗震怒，切責阿林保，謂：「朕若輕信其言，豈不自失良將？

translations.literal: The Renzong Emperor was greatly angered and sharply rebuked Alinbao, saying: "If We lightly believed his words, would We not have lost a fine general of Our own accord?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong was furious and sharply rebuked Alinbao: "Had I believed him lightly, I would have lost a fine general through my own fault.

sentences.zh: 嗣後勦賊專倚長庚，儻阿林保從中掣肘，玉德即前車之鑑！

translations.literal: Henceforth in suppressing the pirates rely solely on Changgeng; if Alinbao obstructs from within, Yude is the warning from the cart ahead!
translations.idiomatic: Hereafter the pirate campaign will rest solely on Changgeng. If Alinbao hampers him from within, let Yude's fate be your warning!"

sentences.zh: 」並飭造大同安梭船三十，未成以前，先僱商船備剿。

translations.literal: " He also ordered thirty Datong'an sloop warships built; before they were finished, merchant vessels were first hired for suppression.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered thirty Datong'an sloop warships built and, until they were ready, hired merchant ships for the campaign.

sentences.zh: 長庚聞之，益感奮。

translations.literal: When Changgeng heard this he was all the more moved and inspired.
translations.idiomatic: Changgeng was stirred to still greater zeal when he heard this.

sentences.zh: 是年秋，擊賊於漁山，受傷，事聞，復還翎頂。

translations.literal: That autumn he attacked the pirates at Yushan and was wounded; when the matter was reported, his feather and insignia were restored.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he fought the pirates at Yushan and was wounded. When the court learned of it, his peacock feather and insignia were restored.

sentences.zh: 十二年春，擊敗牽於粵洋大星嶼。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twelfth year he defeated Qian at Daxing Island in Guangdong waters.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of year 12 he defeated Cai Qian off Daxing Island in Guangdong waters.

sentences.zh: 十一月，又擊敗於閩洋浮鷹山。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he defeated him again at Fuying Mountain in Fujian waters.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he beat him again off Fuying Mountain in Fujian waters.

sentences.zh: 十二月，遂偕福建提督張見升追牽入澳，窮其所向，至黑水洋。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he then joined Fujian Commander Zhang Jiansheng in pursuing Qian into the outer sea, following him to the end of his course as far as the Black Water Sea.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he and Fujian Commander Zhang Jiansheng chased Cai Qian into the open ocean and followed him all the way to the Black Water Sea.

sentences.zh: 牽僅存三艇，皆百戰之寇，以死拒。

translations.literal: Qian had only three junks left, all veteran fighters who resisted to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Qian had only three junks left, manned by veterans who fought to the death.

sentences.zh: 長庚自以火攻船掛其艇尾，欲躍登，忽砲中喉，移時而殞。

translations.literal: Changgeng himself took a fire-attack ship and hooked it to the stern of Qian's junk, intending to leap aboard; suddenly a cannon ball struck his throat and after a time he died.
translations.idiomatic: Changgeng himself brought a fire ship alongside the stern of Qian's junk to board, when a cannon ball struck his throat. He died shortly after.

sentences.zh: 時戰艦數十倍於賊，見升庸懦，遙見總統船亂，遽退，牽乃遁入安南外洋。

translations.literal: At the time the war fleet was many times the pirates' strength, but Jiansheng was timid and cowardly; seeing the commander-in-chief's ship in disorder from afar, he hastily withdrew, and Qian escaped into the outer sea off Annam.
translations.idiomatic: The government fleet outnumbered the pirates many times over, but Zhang Jiansheng was timid. Seeing the flagship in disorder from a distance, he withdrew at once, and Cai Qian escaped toward the open sea off Annam.

sentences.zh: 上震悼，褒血卩，初擬俟寇平錫以伯爵，乃追封三等壯烈伯，諡忠毅，於原籍建專祠。

translations.literal: The Emperor was deeply shaken and mourned him, bestowing posthumous honors; it had originally been planned to ennoble him as a count when the bandits were pacified, but he was posthumously enfeoffed as Baron of the Third Rank, Zhuanglie, with the posthumous title Zhongyi, and a special shrine was built in his native place.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor mourned him deeply and granted posthumous honors. He had been slated for a countship once the pirates were destroyed; instead he was posthumously made Baron Zhuanglie of the third rank, with the temple name Zhongyi, and a shrine was built in his home district.

sentences.zh: 長庚治軍嚴，信賞必罰，自偏裨下至隊長水手，耳目心志如一，人人皆可用。

translations.literal: Changgeng governed the army strictly, keeping faith in rewards and certain in punishments; from deputy commanders down to squad leaders and sailors, ears, eyes, and minds were as one, and every man could be put to use.
translations.idiomatic: Changgeng ran a strict command, rewarding faithfully and punishing surely. From his deputies down to squad leaders and sailors, every man moved as one will, and each was fit for duty.

sentences.zh: 與阮元同心整厲水師，數建功，為玉德所忌。

translations.literal: With Ruan Yuan he worked in concert to reform and strengthen the navy, won merit many times, and was envied by Yude.
translations.idiomatic: He and Ruan Yuan worked together to rebuild the navy, won repeated victories, and earned Yude's jealousy.

sentences.zh: 及阿林保之至閩也，置酒款長庚，謂曰：「大海捕魚，何時入網？

translations.literal: When Alinbao came to Fujian he set out wine to entertain Changgeng and said: "Fishing in the great sea—when will the fish enter the net?
translations.idiomatic: When Alinbao reached Fujian he entertained Changgeng with wine and said, "Fishing the open sea—who knows when the net will fill?

sentences.zh: 海外事無左證，公但斬一酋，以牽首報，我飛章告捷，以餘賊歸善後辦理。

translations.literal: Overseas affairs have no corroborating witnesses; you need only behead one chieftain and report it as Qian's head. I will dispatch a rapid memorial announcing victory, and leave the remaining bandits for later settlement.
translations.idiomatic: At sea there are no witnesses. Behead one leader, call it Cai Qian's head, and I will rush a victory report to court. We can tidy up the rest later.

sentences.zh: 公受上賞，我亦邀次功，孰與窮年冒風濤僥倖萬一哉？

translations.literal: You receive the highest reward and I also claim a secondary merit—how does that compare with spending years braving wind and waves for a one-in-ten-thousand chance?
translations.idiomatic: You take the top honors and I share the credit—surely that beats spending years in storms for a one-in-ten-thousand chance?"

sentences.zh: 」長庚謝曰：「吾何能為此？

translations.literal: " Changgeng declined and said: "How could I do such a thing?
translations.idiomatic: Changgeng refused: "How could I do such a thing?

sentences.zh: 久視海船如廬舍，誓與賊同死，不與同生！

translations.literal: I have long regarded a ship at sea as my home; I swear to die with the bandits and not to live with them!
translations.idiomatic: I have long made a ship my home. I swear to die with these pirates rather than let them live!"

sentences.zh: 」阿林保不懌。

translations.literal: " Alinbao was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Alinbao took offense.

sentences.zh: 既屢劾不得逞，則飛檄趣戰。

translations.literal: When repeated impeachments failed, he sent urgent dispatches pressing for battle.
translations.idiomatic: When his repeated accusations failed, he sent urgent orders demanding battle.

sentences.zh: 長庚緘所落齒寄其妻，志以身殉國。

translations.literal: Changgeng sealed the teeth he had lost and sent them to his wife, resolved to give his life for the state.
translations.idiomatic: Changgeng sent his wife the teeth he had lost in battle, resolved to die for the throne.

sentences.zh: 既歿，詔部將王得祿、邱良功嗣任，勉以同心敵愾​​，為長庚雪仇。

translations.literal: After his death an edict ordered his subordinates Wang Delu and Qiu Lianggong to succeed him, urging them to unite in hatred of the common foe and avenge Changgeng.
translations.idiomatic: After his death the court ordered his lieutenants Wang Delu and Qiu Lianggong to take up his command, urging them to stand together against the enemy and avenge Changgeng.

sentences.zh: 二人遵其部勒，卒滅蔡牽，竟全功焉。

translations.literal: The two men followed his dispositions and in the end destroyed Cai Qian, fully completing the achievement.
translations.idiomatic: They followed his battle plans, destroyed Cai Qian in the end, and brought the campaign to full success.

sentences.zh: 長庚無子，養同姓子廷鈺為嗣，襲伯爵，授二等侍衛。

translations.literal: Changgeng had no son; he adopted a clansman named Tingyu as heir, who inherited the barony and was appointed a Second-Rank Bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: Changgeng had no son of his own and adopted a kinsman, Tingyu, as heir. Tingyu inherited the barony and was appointed a Second-Rank Bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 道光中，出為南昌副將，累擢浙江提督。

translations.literal: In the Daoguang reign he went out as deputy commander at Nanchang and was repeatedly promoted to naval commander-in-chief of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Daoguang he served as deputy commander at Nanchang and rose in due course to naval commander-in-chief of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 因病不能巡洋，奪職家居。

translations.literal: Because of illness he could not patrol the seas; his post was taken away and he lived at home.
translations.idiomatic: Illness kept him from patrolling the coast, his post was revoked, and he retired to his home.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，治本籍團練，迭克廈門、金島、仙遊，授福建提督。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianfeng he organized local militia in his native district, repeatedly captured Xiamen, Jindao, and Xianyou, and was appointed naval commander-in-chief of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianfeng he raised militia in his home district, recaptured Xiamen, Jindao, and Xianyou in succession, and was made naval commander-in-chief of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 尋以誤報軍情解任，仍會辦團練。

translations.literal: Soon he was dismissed for misreporting military intelligence but continued to assist in organizing the militia.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon removed for misreporting the military situation but continued to help organize the militia.

sentences.zh: 十一年，卒，孫經寶襲爵。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he died; his grandson Jingbao inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11 he died, and his grandson Jingbao inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 胡振聲，亦同安人，提督貴子。

translations.literal: Hu Zhensheng was also a native of Tong'an and a son of the noble house of a commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zhensheng, also from Tong'an, was the son of a commander-in-chief's ennobled family.

sentences.zh: 起行伍，累擢至溫州鎮總兵。

translations.literal: He rose from the ranks and was repeatedly promoted to commander of the Wenzhou Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to commander of the Wenzhou Garrison.

sentences.zh: 從長庚大破夷艇於台州松門洋，自是屢從長庚擊賊海上。

translations.literal: He followed Changgeng in inflicting a great defeat on foreign rebel vessels at Songmenyang off Taizhou, and from then on repeatedly followed Changgeng in attacking pirates at sea.
translations.idiomatic: He fought with Changgeng in the great victory over foreign rebel junks at Songmenyang off Taizhou and thereafter joined him in many sea campaigns.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶九年六月，率二十六艘運舟材赴福建，至浮鷹洋，遇賊，與總兵孫大剛夾攻，殲賊甚眾，而舟為砲焚，閩師不能救，遂被害。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the ninth year of Jiaqing he led twenty-six ships carrying timber for vessels to Fujian; at Fuyingyang they met pirates, and with Brigade General Sun Dagang attacked from both sides, destroying many of the enemy, but his ship was burned by cannon fire and the Fujian fleet could not save him, and he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Jiaqing 9 he led twenty-six ships carrying ship timber to Fujian. At Fuyingyang they met pirates; he and Brigade General Sun Dagang attacked from both sides and destroyed many, but his vessel was set afire by cannon shot. The Fujian fleet could not reach him, and he was killed.

sentences.zh: 優恤，諡武壯，予騎都尉兼雲騎尉世職。

translations.literal: He was given generous condolence rewards, granted the posthumous title Wuzhuang, and awarded the hereditary offices of Cavalry Commandant and Cloud Cavalry Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted generous posthumous honors, gave him the temple name Wuzhuang, and awarded hereditary ranks as Cavalry Commandant and Cloud Cavalry Commandant.

sentences.zh: 王得祿，字玉峰，福建嘉義人。

translations.literal: Wang Delu, style name Yufeng, was a native of Jiayi in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Delu, whose style was Yufeng, came from Jiayi in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 林爽文倡亂，陷縣城。

translations.literal: Lin Shuangwen raised a rebellion and captured the county seat.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin Shuangwen rebelled, the county seat fell.

sentences.zh: 得祿家素豐，捐貲募鄉勇，助官軍復之，授把總。

translations.literal: Delu's family was wealthy; he donated funds to raise local militia, aided the government army in recovering the city, and was appointed a platoon leader.
translations.idiomatic: Delu's family was wealthy. He donated funds, raised local militia, helped the government recover the city, and was made a platoon leader.

sentences.zh: 明年，賊复圍城，從總兵柴大紀固守。

translations.literal: The next year the rebels again besieged the city; he followed Brigade General Chai Daji in a stubborn defense.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the rebels besieged the city again. He served under Brigade General Chai Daji in a stubborn defense.

sentences.zh: 及圍解，率鄉勇搜捕大坪頂等處餘匪，焚瑯嶠賊巢，賊渠莊大田就擒。

translations.literal: When the siege was lifted he led local militia to hunt down remaining bandits at Dapingding and elsewhere, burned the rebel nest at Langjiao, and the bandit leader Zhuang Datian was captured.
translations.idiomatic: After the siege was raised he led militia against remnant rebels at Dapingding and elsewhere, burned the nest at Langjiao, and the bandit chief Zhuang Datian was taken.

sentences.zh: 台灣平，賜花翎、五品頂戴，遷千總。

translations.literal: When Taiwan was pacified he was granted the peacock feather and fifth-rank insignia and was promoted to company commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiwan was pacified he received the peacock feather and fifth-rank insignia and was promoted to company commander.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年，巡洋至獺窟，遇賊，得祿先登，擒吳興信等。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing, while patrolling the coast he reached Takou, met pirates, and Delu was first to board and captured Wu Xingxin and others.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 1, while on coastal patrol he reached Takou, met pirates, boarded first, and captured Wu Xingxin and others.

sentences.zh: 歷年出洋捕海盜，號勇敢，累擢金門營游擊。

translations.literal: Over the years he went out to sea to hunt pirates, was known for bravery, and was repeatedly promoted to acting commander of the Kinmen battalion.
translations.idiomatic: Year after year he put to sea against pirates, earning a reputation for courage, and rose through repeated promotions until he was acting commander of the Kinmen battalion.

sentences.zh: 七年，從李長庚擊蔡牽於東滬洋，擒賊目徐業等百餘人，又擒呂送於崇武洋，被獎敘。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he followed Li Changgeng in attacking Cai Qian at the Donghu Sea, captured more than a hundred bandits including the chieftain Xu Ye, and also captured Lü Song at the Chongwu Sea; he was rewarded for his merit.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 7 he fought under Li Changgeng against Cai Qian in the Donghu Sea, taking more than a hundred pirates including the chieftain Xu Ye, and later captured Lü Song in the Chongwu Sea. His merit was duly recorded.

sentences.zh: 九年，從總兵羅仁太擊賊於虎頭山洋面，獲船械甚多。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he followed Brigade General Luo Rentai in attacking bandits on the waters off Hutoushan and seized a great many ships and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 9 he joined Brigade General Luo Rentai in fighting pirates off Hutoushan and captured a large quantity of ships and arms.

sentences.zh: 十年，擊蔡牽於虎井洋，敗之，署澎湖協副將。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he attacked Cai Qian at the Hujing Sea, defeated him, and was appointed acting deputy commander of the Penghu garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 10 he defeated Cai Qian at the Hujing Sea and was made acting deputy commander of the Penghu garrison.

sentences.zh: 九月，遇牽於水澳，焚其舟，擒殲硃列等百餘人。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he encountered Qian at Shui'ao, burned their ships, and captured and killed more than a hundred men including Zhu Lie.
translations.idiomatic: That September he cornered Qian at Shui'ao, burned his fleet, and killed or captured more than a hundred of his men, including Zhu Lie.

sentences.zh: 十一年春，牽入台灣，圍府城。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eleventh year Qian entered Taiwan and besieged the prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Jiaqing 11, Qian invaded Taiwan and laid siege to the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 李長庚令得祿與許松年駕小舟自安平港入偵之，帆檣彌望，夜縱火焚賊舟，遂入屯柴頭港。

translations.literal: Li Changgeng ordered Delu and Xu Songnian to take small boats from Anping Harbor to scout; sails and masts filled the view as far as the eye could see. At night they set fires and burned the bandit ships, then entered and encamped at Chaitou Harbor.
translations.idiomatic: Li Changgeng sent Delu and Xu Songnian in small boats from Anping Harbor to reconnoiter. The horizon was thick with sails and masts. That night they set the pirate ships ablaze and then moved inland to camp at Chaitou Harbor.

sentences.zh: 明日，賊自洲仔尾攻府城北門，得祿率兵躡其後，大呼以前，賊驚卻。

translations.literal: The next day the bandits attacked the north gate of the prefectural city from Zhouzaiwei. Delu led troops in pursuit from behind, shouting as he pressed forward, and the bandits were startled and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the rebels struck the city's north gate from Zhouzaiwei. Delu came up from behind at a run, shouting as he charged, and the startled pirates fell back.

sentences.zh: 城內軍出夾攻，大敗之，乘勝至洲仔尾，破其營，賊乃遁。

translations.literal: Troops from inside the city came out and attacked from both sides, inflicting a great defeat. Pressing the advantage they reached Zhouzaiwei, smashed the bandit camp, and the bandits then fled.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison sallied forth to attack from both sides and routed them. The victors pressed on to Zhouzaiwei, destroyed the rebel camp, and the pirates fled.

sentences.zh: 五月，牽复竄鹿耳門，得祿首先沖擊，獲船十，沈船十一。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Qian again fled to Luerhmen. Delu was first to charge and seized ten ships while sinking eleven.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Qian slipped back to Luerhmen. Delu led the assault, capturing ten ships and sinking eleven.

sentences.zh: 敘功，加總兵銜。

translations.literal: His merits were recorded and he was given the rank of brigade general.
translations.idiomatic: His deeds were entered in the merit rolls and he received brigade-general rank.

sentences.zh: 尋擢福寧鎮總兵。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was promoted to brigade general of Funing Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to brigade general of the Funing garrison.

sentences.zh: 十二年，調南澳鎮。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was transferred to the Nan'ao garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 12 he was transferred to command the Nan'ao garrison.

sentences.zh: 七月，敗硃濆於雞籠洋，獲船十四。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he defeated Zhu Fen at the Jilong Sea and captured fourteen ships.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he routed Zhu Fen in the Jilong Sea and took fourteen ships.

sentences.zh: 十一月，又敗其黨於古雷洋，射殪賊目硃金，擒張祈，被獎敘。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he again defeated Zhu Fen's followers at the Gulei Sea, shot and killed the bandit chieftain Zhu Jin, captured Zhang Qi, and was rewarded for his merit.
translations.idiomatic: That November he defeated Zhu Fen's faction again in the Gulei Sea, shot down the pirate chief Zhu Jin, captured Zhang Qi, and received an official commendation.

sentences.zh: 未幾，李長庚戰歿，命得祿與邱良功繼任軍事。

translations.literal: Before long Li Changgeng died in battle, and Delu and Qiu Lianggong were ordered to take over military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after, Li Changgeng fell in battle, and Delu and Qiu Lianggong were ordered to succeed him in the campaign.

sentences.zh: 十三年，擢浙江提督。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was promoted to provincial military commander of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 13 he was promoted to provincial military commander of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 既而調福建，邱良功代之。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to Fujian, and Qiu Lianggong replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Fujian, with Qiu Lianggong taking his former post.

sentences.zh: 時阮元再任浙江巡撫，張師誠為福建巡撫，兩省合力，得祿與良功同心滅賊。

translations.literal: At that time Ruan Yuan was again serving as governor of Zhejiang and Zhang Shicheng was governor of Fujian. The two provinces combined forces, and Delu and Lianggong united in purpose to exterminate the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Yuan had returned as governor of Zhejiang and Zhang Shicheng governed Fujian. With the two provinces acting together, Delu and Lianggong joined forces in a shared determination to wipe out the pirates.

sentences.zh: 十四年八月，同擊蔡牽於定海漁山，敗之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fourteenth year they jointly attacked Cai Qian at Yushan off Dinghai and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Jiaqing 14 they jointly attacked Cai Qian off Yushan near Dinghai and put him to flight.

sentences.zh: 牽東南走，追至黑水洋，合擊累日，良功以浙舟駢列賊舟東，得祿率閩舟列浙舟東，戰酣，良功舟傷暫退，得祿舟進，附牽舟，諸賊黨隔不得援。

translations.literal: Qian fled southeast and they pursued him to the Black Water Sea, where they fought together for days. Lianggong arrayed Zhejiang ships abreast east of Qian's fleet, while Delu led Fujian ships in line east of the Zhejiang vessels. As the battle grew fierce, Lianggong's ship was damaged and he withdrew briefly; Delu's ship advanced and came alongside Qian's, so the bandit followers could not come to his aid across the gap.
translations.idiomatic: Qian fled southeast; they pursued him to the Black Water Sea and fought jointly for days. Lianggong lined the Zhejiang fleet abreast to the east of Qian's ships, while Delu deployed Fujian vessels east of the Zhejiang line. In the heat of battle Lianggong's ship was crippled and he pulled back briefly. Delu pressed forward, locked alongside Qian's vessel, and cut off the pirate lieutenants from reaching him.

sentences.zh: 牽鉛丸盡，以番銀代，得祿額腕皆傷，擲火焚牽舟尾樓，复衝斷其柁。

translations.literal: Qian exhausted his lead shot and used foreign silver coins instead. Delu was wounded on forehead and wrist, hurled fire to burn the aftercastle of Qian's ship, and again charged and broke its rudder.
translations.idiomatic: Qian ran out of lead shot and fired foreign silver coins instead. Delu took wounds to his brow and wrist, threw fire onto the stern tower of Qian's ship, and rammed again, snapping the rudder.

sentences.zh: 牽知不免，舉砲自裂其舟沉於海。

translations.literal: Qian knew he could not escape; he raised a cannon and blew apart his own ship, which sank into the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing no way out, Qian turned his cannon on his own vessel and blew it apart, sending it to the bottom.

sentences.zh: 詔以牽肆逆十有四年，渠魁就殲，厥功甚偉，錫封得祿二等子爵，賜雙眼花翎。

translations.literal: An edict stated that Qian had rebelled for fourteen years and that the ringleader had now been destroyed—a feat of great magnitude. Delu was enfeoffed as a second-class viscount and granted the double-eyed peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict noted that Qian had rebelled for fourteen years and that at last the chief was destroyed—a signal achievement. Delu was enfeoffed as a second-class viscount and honored with the double-eyed peacock plume.

sentences.zh: 餘黨千二百人，後皆降，海盜遂息。

translations.literal: The remaining followers, twelve hundred men, all surrendered afterward, and piracy on the seas then subsided.
translations.idiomatic: The twelve hundred survivors eventually surrendered, and piracy on the coast subsided.

sentences.zh: 得祿為福建提督歷十載，屢疏陳緝捕事宜，改定水師船制，皆如議行。

translations.literal: Delu served as provincial military commander of Fujian for ten years, repeatedly memorializing on matters of pursuit and capture, and reforming the naval ship regulations—all of which were approved and implemented.
translations.idiomatic: As Fujian's provincial commander for ten years, Delu repeatedly memorialized on anti-piracy measures and reforms to the naval fleet, and his proposals were adopted.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，調浙江提督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was transferred to provincial military commander of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 25 he was transferred back to provincial military commander of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，乞病歸。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang he requested leave on grounds of illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 1 he retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 十二年，台灣張丙作亂，得祿率家屬擒賊目張紅頭等，加太子少保。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Zhang Bing of Taiwan rebelled. Delu led members of his household in capturing the bandit chieftain Zhang Hongtou and others, and was promoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 12, when Zhang Bing rebelled in Taiwan, Delu and his household captured the rebel chief Zhang Hongtou and others. He was raised to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十八年，台匪沈和肆掠，輸糧助守，晉太子太保。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the Taiwan bandit Shen He rampaged and plundered; Delu supplied grain to aid in the defense and was advanced to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 18, when the Taiwan bandit Shen He went on a rampage, Delu sent grain to support the defense and was promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，英吉利犯廈門，命駐守澎湖。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year England attacked Xiamen, and he was ordered to garrison Penghu.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 21, when the English attacked Xiamen, he was ordered to hold Penghu.

sentences.zh: 次年，卒，贈伯爵，諡果毅。

translations.literal: The next year he died. He was posthumously granted the title of earl and given the posthumous name Guoyi ("Resolute and Decisive").
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year. He was posthumously made an earl and given the posthumous name Guoyi, "Resolute and Decisive."

sentences.zh: 次子朝綸襲子爵，官戶部員外郎。

translations.literal: His second son Chaolun inherited the viscountcy and served as an assistant secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Chaolun inherited the viscountcy and held office as an assistant secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 邱良功，福建同安人。

translations.literal: Qiu Lianggong was a native of Tong'an in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Lianggong came from Tong'an in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 起行伍，屢以獲盜功，洊擢閩安協副將。

translations.literal: He rose from the ranks and, repeatedly rewarded for capturing bandits, was promoted step by step to deputy commander of the Min'an garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He came up through the ranks, and a string of captures earned him steady promotion until he was deputy commander of the Min'an garrison.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十年，偕許松年會剿蔡牽，追至小琉球，見台灣師船二為賊圍，赴援，松年舉旗招之，未至。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Jiaqing he joined Xu Songnian in a joint suppression of Cai Qian and pursued him to Little Ryukyu. He saw two Taiwan government ships surrounded by bandits and went to their aid. Songnian raised flags to summon him, but he did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 10 he joined Xu Songnian in the campaign against Cai Qian and pursued the pirates to Little Ryukyu. Spotting two Taiwan government ships under siege, he sailed to help—but when Songnian signaled him by flag, he failed to rendezvous.

sentences.zh: 以違調遣被劾，褫職逮訊。

translations.literal: He was impeached for disobeying orders, stripped of his rank, and arrested for interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: He was impeached for disobeying orders, dismissed from office, and taken into custody for questioning.

sentences.zh: 得白，復原官，署台灣副將。

translations.literal: He was cleared of wrongdoing, restored to his original office, and appointed acting deputy commander of Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: Exonerated, he was restored to his former rank and made acting deputy commander of Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 十一年春，從李長庚擊蔡牽，破洲仔尾賊巢，牽乘間逸，奪頂戴。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eleventh year he followed Li Changgeng in attacking Cai Qian, destroyed the bandit nest at Zhouzaiwei, but Qian slipped away in an interval and Lianggong's rank insignia was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Jiaqing 11 he fought under Li Changgeng against Cai Qian and destroyed the nest at Zhouzaiwei—but Qian escaped in the confusion, and Lianggong lost his rank insignia as punishment.

sentences.zh: 五月，破牽於鹿耳門，賜花翎。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he defeated Qian at Luerhmen and was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he routed Qian at Luerhmen and was awarded the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 十二年，硃濆犯淡水，偕王得祿追至雞籠洋，連敗之，擒殲甚眾，被優敘。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Zhu Fen invaded Tamsui. Together with Wang Delu he pursued him to the Jilong Sea, defeated him repeatedly, captured and killed a great many, and received an outstanding commendation.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 12, when Zhu Fen struck Tamsui, he and Wang Delu pursued him to the Jilong Sea, defeated him in successive engagements, killed or captured a great number, and earned special commendation.

sentences.zh: 十三年，擢浙江定海鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was promoted to brigade general of the Dinghai garrison in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 13 he was promoted to brigade general of the Dinghai garrison in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 十四年，擢浙江提督。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was promoted to provincial military commander of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 14 he was made provincial military commander of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 偕王得祿合擊蔡牽於漁山外洋，乘上風逼之，夜半浪急，不得進。

translations.literal: Together with Wang Delu he jointly attacked Cai Qian on the open sea off Yushan, using the windward advantage to press him, but at midnight the waves grew fierce and they could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: With Wang Delu he attacked Cai Qian in the open sea off Yushan, riding the wind to press him—but at midnight the seas turned rough and they could not close.

sentences.zh: 明日，复要截環攻，牽且戰且走，傍午逾黑水洋，見綠水。

translations.literal: The next day they again sought to intercept and surround him in attack. Qian fought as he fled, and by noon they had crossed the Black Water Sea and saw green water.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they tried again to block and surround him. Qian fought his way eastward, and by noon they had passed the Black Water Sea into open blue water.

sentences.zh: 良功恐日暮賊遁，大呼突進，以己舟逼牽舟，兩篷相結。

translations.literal: Lianggong feared the bandits would escape at dusk; he shouted and charged forward, pressing his ship against Qian's until the two sails entangled.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Qian would escape at nightfall, Lianggong shouted and dashed forward, driving his ship against Qian's until their sails became entangled.

sentences.zh: 賊以椗衝船，陷入死鬥。

translations.literal: The bandits used grappling anchors to ram the ship, and both sides were locked in a fight to the death.
translations.idiomatic: The pirates grappled with anchors and rammed his ship, and the two crews were locked in a fight to the death.

sentences.zh: 良功腓被矛傷，毀賊椗，得脫出。

translations.literal: Lianggong's calf was wounded by a spear; he destroyed the bandits' grappling anchor and was able to break free.
translations.idiomatic: A spear pierced Lianggong's calf, but he smashed the pirates' grappling gear and broke free.

sentences.zh: 閩師繼之，牽遂裂舟自沉。

translations.literal: The Fujian fleet followed up, and Qian then split open his ship and sank himself.
translations.idiomatic: The Fujian fleet pressed the attack, and Qian scuttled his own vessel.

sentences.zh: 論功，錫封三等男爵，次於王得祿。

translations.literal: When merits were assessed he was enfeoffed as a third-class baron, ranking below Wang Delu.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was enfeoffed as a third-class baron—one rank below Wang Delu.

sentences.zh: 或為之不平，良功曰：「海疆肅清，已為快事，名位軒輊何足計？

translations.literal: Some considered it unfair on his behalf; Lianggong said: "The sea frontier has been cleared and pacified—that is already a cause for joy; how can differences in rank and position be worth reckoning?
translations.idiomatic: Some felt the award slighted him, but Lianggong said, "The seas are cleared—that is joy enough. What do petty differences in rank matter?

sentences.zh: 」二十二年，入覲，卒於途，賜卹，諡剛勇。

translations.literal: " In the twenty-second year he went to audience at court, died on the road, was granted mourning compensation, and was given the posthumous title Gangyong.
translations.idiomatic: " In Jiaqing 22 he set out for court but died on the road; the throne granted condolence funds and the posthumous title Gangyong, Staunch and Brave.

sentences.zh: 子聯恩襲男爵，官直隸河間協副將。

translations.literal: His son Lian'en inherited the baronetcy and served as deputy brigade commander of the Hejian Brigade in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lian'en inherited the baronetcy and held the post of deputy brigade commander of the Hejian Brigade in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 陳步雲，浙江瑞安人。

translations.literal: Chen Buyun was a native of Ruian in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Buyun came from Ruian in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 入伍隸水師，數獲盜，以勇力稱，授溫州營把總。

translations.literal: He enlisted and joined the navy, captured pirates many times, was renowned for his courage and strength, and was appointed platoon leader of the Wenzhou Battalion.
translations.idiomatic: He enlisted in the navy, captured pirates again and again, and won a name for raw courage before he was made platoon leader of the Wenzhou Battalion.

sentences.zh: 從良功追蔡牽，步雲以四十人駕舟徑逼牽艦鏖鬥，舟小不相當，見兩提督至，亟投火罐焚賊艦，以長戟鉤舷，率數卒躍登，短兵相搏，殲牽妻及其黨。

translations.literal: Following Lianggong in pursuit of Cai Qian, Buyun took forty men in a boat and drove straight at Qian's flagship for a fierce fight; their vessel was too small to be an equal match; when he saw the two admirals arrive, he urgently cast fire pots to burn the pirate ship, hooked the rail with a long halberd, led several soldiers in a leap aboard, fought at close quarters, and annihilated Qian's wife and her followers.
translations.idiomatic: When Lianggong pursued Cai Qian, Buyun put forty men in a boat and rowed straight at the pirate flagship. His craft was far too small for a fair fight, but as the two admirals came up he hurled fire pots onto the enemy deck, hooked the rail with a long halberd, and led a handful of men over the side. In close combat they killed Qian's wife and her band.

sentences.zh: 賊艦已壞，牽猶持利刃踞柁樓，顧欲取之。

translations.literal: The pirate ship was already damaged, but Qian still grasped a sharp blade and crouched on the helm tower, looking back as if he meant to take him.
translations.idiomatic: The pirate ship was already breaking up, yet Qian still crouched on the helm tower with a naked blade, turning as though he meant to cut Buyun down.

sentences.zh: 良功隔船疾呼，船與水平，速去，放長繩水中援之起，而牽船沒矣。

translations.literal: Lianggong shouted urgently across the boats: "Level the ship with the water surface—get away quickly!" He lowered a long rope into the water to pull him up, and Qian's ship sank.
translations.idiomatic: Lianggong shouted from the next boat: "Trim her to the waterline and get clear!" He dropped a long rope into the sea and hauled Buyun up just as Qian's vessel went under.

sentences.zh: 步雲身被十數創，兩提督皆臨慰視。

translations.literal: Buyun's body sustained more than ten wounds; both admirals came in person to comfort and examine him.
translations.idiomatic: Buyun had taken more than a dozen wounds, and both admirals came aboard to comfort him and see to his injuries.

sentences.zh: 事聞，賜獎武銀牌，擢千總。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, he was awarded a military commendation silver plaque and promoted to company commander.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the throne, he received a silver commendation plaque for valor and was promoted to company commander.

sentences.zh: 累遷閩安副將。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted until he became deputy commander of the Min'an Brigade.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in due course to deputy commander of the Min'an Brigade.

sentences.zh: 總督孫爾準欲裁減師船，步雲言李提督所造船高大堅緻，其利遠勝同安夾板、快駒諸船、裁之緝匪無具，有事不能制敵，議乃寢。

translations.literal: Governor-General Sun Erzhun wished to cut and reduce the fleet ships; Buyun said that the vessels built under Admiral Li were tall, large, solid, and fine—their advantage far exceeded those like the Tong'an double-planked ships and Kuaiju fast boats; if they were cut back there would be no equipment for suppressing bandits, and when trouble arose they could not control the enemy; the proposal was then shelved.
translations.idiomatic: When Governor-General Sun Erzhun proposed trimming the fleet, Buyun argued that the ships Admiral Li had built were tall, stout, and finely made—far superior to Tong'an double-planked craft and Kuaiju runners. Cut them and the navy would lack the tools to hunt pirates and could not hold an enemy in a crisis. The plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 爾準薦其才可勝專閫，入覲，宣宗曰：「汝即隨邱、王兩提督攻沉蔡牽之陳步雲耶？

translations.literal: Erzhun recommended that his talent could fill an independent command; on appearing at court audience, the Daoguang Emperor said: "Are you Chen Buyun, who followed Admirals Qiu and Wang to attack and sink Cai Qian?
translations.idiomatic: Erzhun recommended him as fit for independent command. At court the Daoguang Emperor asked, "Are you Chen Buyun—the man who followed Admirals Qiu and Wang and helped sink Cai Qian?

sentences.zh: 」詢戰功甚悉。

translations.literal: " He questioned him very thoroughly about his battle achievements.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor questioned him closely about the fight.

sentences.zh: 遂擢定海鎮總兵，歷瓊州、福寧、金門、海壇諸鎮。

translations.literal: He was then promoted to commander of the Dinghai Garrison and successively held commands at Qiongzhou, Funing, Jinmen, and Haitan.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made commander of the Dinghai Garrison and went on to hold the garrisons at Qiongzhou, Funing, Jinmen, and Haitan.

sentences.zh: 道光十九年，以傷發，乞解職。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Daoguang, his old wounds flared up and he requested to resign his post.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 19 his old wounds reopened and he asked to be relieved of duty.

sentences.zh: 三十年，卒。

translations.literal: In year thirty he died.
translations.idiomatic: In year 30 he died.

sentences.zh: 許松年，字蓉俊，浙江瑞安人。

translations.literal: Xu Songnian, style name Rongjun, was a native of Ruian in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Songnian, whose style was Rongjun, came from Ruian in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 以武舉效力水師，從李長庚積功至提標參將。

translations.literal: Having passed the military provincial examination, he served in the navy; following Li Changgeng he accumulated merit until he reached the rank of brigade general under the admiral's banner.
translations.idiomatic: After taking his degree as a military licentiate he entered the navy; serving under Li Changgeng he rose on merit to brigade general on the admiral's staff.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十年，護理金門鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Jiaqing he acted as commander of the Jinmen Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 10 he served as acting commander of the Jinmen Garrison.

sentences.zh: 擊蔡牽於小琉球；

translations.literal: He fought Cai Qian at Lesser Ryukyu;
translations.idiomatic: He fought Cai Qian off Lesser Ryukyu;

sentences.zh: 又擊硃濆、烏石二於宮仔洋，從李長庚追敗之於閩、粵交界甲子洋。

translations.literal: He also fought Zhu Fen and Wushi II at Gongzai Bay, and following Li Changgeng pursued and defeated them at Jiazi Bay on the Fujian-Guangdong border.
translations.idiomatic: He also engaged Zhu Fen and Wushi II in Gongzai Bay and, with Li Changgeng in pursuit, routed them at Jiazi Bay where Fujian meets Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 又迭擊牽於青龍港、斗米洋。

translations.literal: He again repeatedly fought Qian at Qinglong Harbor and Doumi Bay.
translations.idiomatic: He clashed with Qian again and again at Qinglong Harbor and Doumi Bay.

sentences.zh: 十一年，偕王得祿敗牽於台灣洲仔尾，跐海水而登，焚溺無算。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, together with Wang Delu he defeated Qian at Zhouziwei in Taiwan, wading through seawater to go ashore; those burned and drowned were beyond count.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11 he and Wang Delu beat Qian at Zhouziwei in Taiwan, wading through the surf to land; the pirates burned and drowned were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 是年夏，李長庚攻牽於鹿耳門，松年扼張坑、返埕洋面，獲賊船一，沉船三，又於水澳擒蔡三來等。

translations.literal: That summer, Li Changgeng attacked Qian at Lu'ermen; Songnian blocked the waters off Zhangkeng and Fancheng, captured one pirate ship and sank three, and at Shui'ao also captured Cai Sanlai and others.
translations.idiomatic: That summer Li Changgeng struck Qian at Lu'ermen while Songnian held the waters off Zhangkeng and Fancheng, taking one pirate vessel and sinking three; at Shui'ao he also captured Cai Sanlai and his men.

sentences.zh: 李長庚論水師將材，舉松年可獨當一面，總督阿林保以疏聞。

translations.literal: Li Changgeng, discussing naval commanders' talent, cited Songnian as one who could hold a front alone; Governor-General A Linbao reported this by memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Appraising the navy's officers, Li Changgeng named Songnian as a man who could hold a sector on his own; Governor-General A Linbao passed the recommendation up by memorial.

sentences.zh: 十二年，從長庚擊蔡牽於大星嶼、浮鷹洋，松年躍入賊船獲之，被優敘。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, following Changgeng he fought Cai Qian at Daxing Isle and Fuying Bay; Songnian leaped into a pirate ship and captured it, and was rewarded with preferential commendation.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12 he followed Changgeng against Cai Qian at Daxing Isle and Fuying Bay; Songnian boarded an enemy vessel and took it, earning a special commendation.

sentences.zh: 十三年，硃濆潛匿東涌外洋，命松年躡剿，遂移師入粵。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Zhu Fen lay concealed in the outer seas off Dongyong; Songnian was ordered to track and suppress him, and the army was then shifted into Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 Zhu Fen hid in the open waters off Dongyong; Songnian was sent to hunt him down and the fleet crossed into Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 追至長山尾，了見賊船四十餘，知其最巨者為濆所乘，並力圍攻，濆受砲傷，未幾斃。

translations.literal: Pursuing to Changshanwei, they clearly saw more than forty pirate ships and knew the largest was the one Fen rode; they combined forces to besiege and attack; Fen received gun wounds and before long died.
translations.idiomatic: At Changshanwei they sighted more than forty pirate junks and closed on the largest, which Fen himself commanded. Under combined fire Fen was hit by cannon; he died soon after.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉松年奮勇，克殲渠魁，賜花翎，予雲騎尉世職。

translations.literal: An edict praised Songnian's valor in decisively destroying the ringleader, granted him the peacock feather, and awarded the hereditary rank of Cloud Cavalry Commander.
translations.idiomatic: The throne praised Songnian's daring in destroying the chief bandit, granted him the peacock feather, and gave him the hereditary rank of Cloud Cavalry Commander.

sentences.zh: 粵匪張保仔竄閩洋金門、廈門，松年遣漁船誘之，以舟師圍擊，獲船七，沉船六，被優敘。

translations.literal: The Guangdong bandit Zhang Baozai fled to Fujian waters at Jinmen and Xiamen; Songnian sent fishing boats to lure him, surrounded and attacked with the fleet, captured seven ships and sank six, and received preferential commendation.
translations.idiomatic: When the Guangdong outlaw Zhang Baozai slipped into Fujian waters off Jinmen and Xiamen, Songnian used fishing boats as bait and closed with the fleet, taking seven junks and sinking six; he was again singled out for reward.

sentences.zh: 十五年，傷發回籍，尋丁母憂。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, his wounds flared up and he returned home; soon after he entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In year 15 his old wounds reopened and he went home; not long after he entered mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 十九年，授甘肅西寧鎮總兵，歷延綏、漳州、天津、碣石諸鎮。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was appointed commander of the Xining Garrison in Gansu and successively held the garrisons at Yansui, Zhangzhou, Tianjin, and Jieshi.
translations.idiomatic: In year 19 he was made commander of the Xining Garrison in Gansu and later held the garrisons at Yansui, Zhangzhou, Tianjin, and Jieshi.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，擢廣東陸路提督，調福建水師提督。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang he was promoted to Guangdong land forces admiral and transferred to Fujian naval admiral.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 1 he was promoted to land forces admiral of Guangdong and transferred to naval admiral of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 六年，台灣械鬥，松年方閱兵，彈壓解散，總督孫爾準與之不協，尋以治理輕縱，被議褫職，留台效力。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, armed factions clashed in Taiwan; Songnian was just reviewing troops, suppressed and dispersed them; Governor-General Sun Erzhun was at odds with him; soon on grounds of lax governance he was impeached and stripped of rank, remaining in Taiwan to serve.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 faction fighting broke out in Taiwan while Songnian was inspecting troops; he suppressed the mobs and broke them up. Governor-General Sun Erzhun took against him, and soon he was impeached for lax rule, stripped of rank, and kept on the island to serve.

sentences.zh: 乞病歸，卒於家。

translations.literal: He pleaded illness and returned home, and died at his residence.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness, went home, and died there.

sentences.zh: 子錫麟，襲世職。

translations.literal: His son Xilin inherited the hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xilin inherited the hereditary rank.

sentences.zh: 黃標，字殿豪，廣東潮州人。

translations.literal: Huang Biao, style name Dianhao, was a native of Chaozhou in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Biao, whose style was Dianhao, came from Chaozhou in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 由行伍拔補千總，擢守備。

translations.literal: From the ranks he was selected and made up to company commander and promoted to battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: Raised from the ranks, he was made company commander and then battalion commander.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五十五年，艇匪肆掠，總督福康安議練水師，募奇才異能者領之。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fifth year of Qianlong, boat bandits rampaged in plunder; Governor-General Fuk'anggan proposed training the navy and recruiting men of unusual talent and ability to lead it.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 55 boat pirates were ravaging the coast; Governor-General Fuk'anggan proposed rebuilding the navy and recruiting exceptional men to command it.

sentences.zh: 標技勇過人，生長海壖，習知水道險易，能久伏水底，視物歷歷可數，特被識拔。

translations.literal: Biao's skill and courage surpassed others; he had grown up on the coastal marshes and was thoroughly familiar with the hazards and advantages of waterways; he could lie submerged for a long time and could count objects clearly; he was specially recognized and selected.
translations.idiomatic: Biao's skill and nerve were extraordinary. Raised on the tidal flats, he knew every shoal and channel; he could stay under water for long stretches and see clearly enough to count what lay below. For this he was singled out.

sentences.zh: 以捕獲龍門洋盜及狗頭山匪功，擢都司，署游擊。

translations.literal: On merit for capturing Longmen Bay pirates and Gou Tou Mountain bandits, he was promoted to battalion director and acted as guerrilla colonel.
translations.idiomatic: For capturing pirates in Longmen Bay and bandits on Gou Tou Mountain he was promoted to battalion director and given acting rank as guerrilla colonel.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年，剿匪於南澎外洋，獲李超勝等三十餘名。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing he suppressed bandits in the outer seas off Nanpeng and captured more than thirty men including Li Chaosheng.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 1 he hunted bandits in the outer waters off Nanpeng and took more than thirty men, including Li Chaosheng.

sentences.zh: 仁宗素知其名，詔嘉緝捕勤能，擢參將。

translations.literal: The Jiaqing Emperor long knew his name; an edict praised his diligence and ability in pursuit and capture, and he was promoted to brigade general.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiaqing Emperor already knew his name; an edict praised his tireless work in pursuit and capture, and he was made brigade general.

sentences.zh: 二年，俘洋盜胡三勝等，复擊斃安南匪首，盡獲其眾，被優敘。

translations.literal: In the second year he captured sea pirates including Hu Sansheng, again struck and killed an Annamese bandit chief, captured all his followers, and was commended with preferential reward.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 he took sea pirates including Hu Sansheng, then killed an Annamese bandit chief and captured his whole band; he received a special commendation.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷澄海副將。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to deputy commander of the Chenghai Brigade.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he was transferred to deputy commander of the Chenghai Brigade.

sentences.zh: 未幾，擢廣東左翼鎮總兵，命總統巡洋水師，責以肅清海盜。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to commander of the Guangdong Left Wing Garrison, ordered to take overall command of the patrol navy, and charged with clearing the seas of pirates.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made commander of the Guangdong Left Wing Garrison, put in overall charge of the patrol fleet, and ordered to clear the seas of pirates.

sentences.zh: 四年，剿匪大放雞山及雙魚桅、夾門外洋，殲獲甚眾，賜花翎，命繪像以進。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he suppressed bandits off Dafangji Mountain and in the outer seas off Shuangyumao and Jiamen; those killed and captured were very numerous; he was granted the peacock feather and ordered to have his portrait painted and presented.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he crushed bandits off Dafangji Mountain and in the waters beyond Shuangyumao and Jiamen, killing and capturing a great host; he received the peacock feather and was ordered to sit for a portrait to be sent to court.

sentences.zh: 尋以盜劫鹽艘被劾，詔原之。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was impeached because pirates had robbed salt transport ships; an edict pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon impeached after pirates robbed a salt convoy, but the throne pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 六年，复擊賊於南澎外洋，獲田亞猛等。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he again fought bandits in the outer seas off Nanpeng and captured Tian Yameng and others.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he fought bandits again in the outer waters off Nanpeng and captured Tian Yameng and his men.

sentences.zh: 七年，偕提督孫全謀剿博羅會匪，連破羊矢坑、羅溪營要隘，搗其巢。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, together with Commander Sun Quanmou he suppressed the Boluo secret-society rebels, successively broke the strategic passes at Yangshikeng and Luoxi Camp, and destroyed their nest.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 he joined Commander Sun Quanmou against the Boluo secret-society rebels, broke the passes at Yangshikeng and Luoxi Camp in succession, and destroyed their stronghold.

sentences.zh: 事平優敘，並被珍賚。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled he received generous merit citation and was also granted imperial gifts.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign he was richly rewarded for merit and received imperial gifts.

sentences.zh: 自將水師，飲食寢處與士卒共，先後獲匪六百餘名，粵海倚為保障。

translations.literal: He personally commanded the navy, sharing food, drink, and quarters with the troops; in all he captured more than six hundred bandits, and the Guangdong seas relied on him as their safeguard.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded the fleet in person, eating and sleeping with his men. In time he took more than six hundred bandits, and Guangdong waters looked to him as their shield.

sentences.zh: 八年，偕孫全謀出海捕賊，賊遁廣州灣。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, together with Sun Quanmou he went to sea to capture pirates; the pirates fled into Guangzhou Bay.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 he and Sun Quanmou put to sea after the pirates, who fled into Guangzhou Bay.

sentences.zh: 標議合兵守隘，俟賊糧盡可盡殲。

translations.literal: Biao proposed uniting the forces to hold the passes and wait until the pirates' grain was exhausted so they could be wholly destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Biao urged a joint blockade of the passes until the pirates starved and could be wiped out.

sentences.zh: 全謀慮持久有風濤患，乃分兵，賊得突圍逸出。

translations.literal: Quanmou feared that a long stand would bring danger from wind and waves, so he divided the troops, and the pirates broke out and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Quanmou feared a long siege would expose the fleet to storms, split his forces, and the pirates broke out and escaped.

sentences.zh: 標歎曰：「此機一失，海警未已！

translations.literal: Biao sighed and said: "Once this chance is lost, alarms at sea will not cease!
translations.idiomatic: Biao sighed, "Miss this chance and the sea will never be quiet!

sentences.zh: 」憤懣成疾。

translations.literal: " Resentment and distress turned into illness.
translations.idiomatic: Resentment and grief brought on illness.

sentences.zh: 尋坐師久無功，吏議奪職留任。

translations.literal: Soon, because the campaign had dragged on without success, the civil officials recommended stripping him of his post while keeping him on duty.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the long campaign without victory led the civil officials to recommend removing his rank while leaving him in post.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died shortly after.

sentences.zh: 自安南夷艇散後，餘黨留粵者分五幫：曰林阿發、曰總兵保、曰郭學顯、曰烏石二、曰鄭乙。

translations.literal: After the Annamese rebel vessels were dispersed, the remnants who stayed in Guangdong divided into five bands: those of Lin Afa, Zongbing Bao, Guo Xuexian, Wushi II, and Zheng Yi.
translations.idiomatic: After the Annamese rebel fleets broke up, the remnants in Guangdong split into five bands: Lin Afa, Zongbing Bao, Guo Xuexian, Wushi II, and Zheng Yi.

sentences.zh: 提督錢夢虎、孫全謀皆庸材，不能辦賊。

translations.literal: Commanders Qian Menghu and Sun Quanmou were both mediocre men who could not deal with the pirates.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders Qian Menghu and Sun Quanmou were mediocre officers who could not suppress the pirates.

sentences.zh: 標歿後，益無良將，惟林國良、許廷桂以死事聞。

translations.literal: After Biao's death there were even fewer capable generals; only Lin Guoliang and Xu Tinggui were famed for dying in service.
translations.idiomatic: After Biao died there were even fewer able commanders; only Lin Guoliang and Xu Tinggui were remembered for dying in battle.

sentences.zh: 國良，福建海澄人。

translations.literal: Guoliang was a native of Haicheng in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Guoliang came from Haicheng in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 世襲騎都尉，授廣東碣石鎮標游擊，累遷海澄副將，繼標為左翼鎮總兵。

translations.literal: He inherited the rank of Cavalry Commandant, was appointed guerrilla colonel of the Jieshi Garrison standard in Guangdong, was repeatedly promoted to deputy commander at Haicheng, and succeeded Biao as commander of the Left Wing Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the rank of Cavalry Commandant, served as guerrilla colonel of the Jieshi standard in Guangdong, rose to deputy commander at Haicheng, and succeeded Biao as commander of the Left Wing Garrison.

sentences.zh: 十三年，追剿烏石二於丫洲洋，擊沉數艘，賊艦續至益多。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he pursued Wushi II to Yazhou Bay, sank several vessels, and pirate ships continued to arrive in ever greater numbers.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 he pursued Wushi II to Yazhou Bay, sank several junks, but pirate ships kept arriving in greater numbers.

sentences.zh: 國良以傷殞，優恤，諡果壯。

translations.literal: Guoliang died of his wounds; he was given generous condolence rewards and granted the posthumous title Guozhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Guoliang died of his wounds. The court granted generous posthumous honors and the temple name Guozhuang.

sentences.zh: 廷桂，廣東歸善人。

translations.literal: Tinggui was a native of Guishan in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Tinggui came from Guishan in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 由行伍擢千總。

translations.literal: From the ranks he was promoted to company commander.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from the ranks to company commander.

sentences.zh: 乾隆中，從征台灣，累遷海門營參將。

translations.literal: In the Qianlong reign he campaigned in Taiwan and was repeatedly promoted to brigade general of the Haimen Garrison.
