translations.idiomatic: Under Qianlong he fought in Taiwan and rose in due course to brigade general of the Haimen Garrison.

sentences.zh: 國良歿，護理左翼鎮總兵。

translations.literal: When Guoliang died he acted as commander of the Left Wing Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin Guoliang died he acted as commander of the Left Wing Garrison.

sentences.zh: 十四年，擊殲匪首總兵保於外洋，圍其餘黨。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he attacked and destroyed the bandit chief Zongbing Bao on the outer sea and besieged the rest of his band.
translations.idiomatic: In year 14 he destroyed the bandit chief Zongbing Bao on the open sea and besieged the rest of his followers.

sentences.zh: 張保仔率大隊來援。

translations.literal: Zhang Baozi led a large force to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Baozi came with a large relief force.

sentences.zh: 眾寡不敵，廷桂死之。

translations.literal: Outnumbered, Tinggui was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Outnumbered, Xu Tinggui was killed.

sentences.zh: 賜卹，予雲騎尉世職。

translations.literal: Condolence rewards were granted and the hereditary office of Cloud Cavalry Commandant was awarded.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted condolence honors and the hereditary rank of Cloud Cavalry Commandant.

sentences.zh: 洎蔡牽既滅，惟粵匪存，於是百齡為兩廣總督，乃斷接濟，整軍紀，越一年，剿撫以次定。

translations.literal: By the time Cai Qian had been destroyed only the Guangdong bandits remained; then Bailin became governor-general of the two Guang provinces, cut off supplies, tightened military discipline, and within a year suppression and pacification settled them in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Once Cai Qian was gone only Guangdong bandits remained. Governor-General Bailin cut off their supplies, tightened discipline, and within a year subdued them by force and persuasion in turn.

sentences.zh: 東南海氛始靖。

translations.literal: The disturbances in the southeast seas were finally pacified.
translations.idiomatic: At last the southeast coast was calm.

sentences.zh: 論曰：東南海寇之擾，始末十有餘年。

translations.literal: The commentators say: The disturbance of the southeast sea bandits lasted from beginning to end more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators observe: The southeast sea pirates plagued the coast for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 惟浙師李長庚一人能辦賊，以閩帥牽掣而阻成功，然長庚忠誠勇略聞於海內，上結主知，廟算既孚，乃專倚畀。

translations.literal: Only Li Changgeng of the Zhejiang fleet could deal with the pirates; Fujian commanders hampered and obstructed his success, yet Changgeng's loyalty, courage, and strategy were known throughout the realm; he won the sovereign's trust, and once court plans were settled the court relied on him alone.
translations.idiomatic: Only Li Changgeng of the Zhejiang fleet could truly fight the pirates, though Fujian commanders hampered him. His loyalty and courage were known throughout the realm; he won the emperor's trust, and once court strategy was set the throne relied on him alone.

sentences.zh: 洎閩、浙合力，賊勢浸衰，不幸長庚中殞，而王得祿、邱良功等以部將承其遺志，卒殲渠魁。

translations.literal: When Fujian and Zhejiang combined their strength the pirates' power gradually waned; unfortunately Changgeng was struck down in mid-career, but Wang Delu, Qiu Lianggong, and others as his subordinates carried on his purpose and in the end destroyed the chief rebel.
translations.idiomatic: When Fujian and Zhejiang joined forces the pirates weakened. Changgeng fell in battle, but Wang Delu, Qiu Lianggong, and other subordinates carried on his purpose and finally destroyed the rebel leader.

sentences.zh: 粵將惟黃標可用，而未盡其才。

translations.literal: Among Guangdong generals only Huang Biao was usable, yet his talent was not fully employed.
translations.idiomatic: Among Guangdong commanders only Huang Biao was truly capable, yet his talent was never fully used.

sentences.zh: 百齡乘閩、浙殄賊之後，剿撫兼施，遂如摧枯拉朽。

translations.literal: Bailin, taking advantage of the time after Fujian and Zhejiang had exterminated the pirates, employed both suppression and pacification, and so it was like breaking dry wood and pulling rotten stakes.
translations.idiomatic: Bailin, after Fujian and Zhejiang had destroyed the main pirate forces, combined suppression with pacification and swept the rest away like dry rot.

sentences.zh: 要之海戰惟恃船堅砲利，與斷接濟而已，循之則勝，違之則敗。

translations.literal: In sum, naval warfare depends only on stout ships and powerful guns, and on cutting off supplies; follow this and you win, violate it and you lose.
translations.idiomatic: In short, naval war depends on strong ships, heavy guns, and cutting off supplies. Follow that path and you win; ignore it and you lose.

sentences.zh: 得失之林，故無幸哉！

translations.literal: The forest of gains and losses—thus there is no luck!
translations.idiomatic: Success and failure follow such a clear pattern that luck has little to do with it.
